en.bestFor: Having one character face the camera full-length and read your own script — announcements, quick updates or presenter-style messages where the outfit and stance should stay visible.
en.structure: The script is split into 1 to 20 clips with a similar word count in each. Each clip is 5–12 seconds at the chosen pace (about 4 Chinese characters or 2.4 English words per second at medium pace).
en.hook: No separate hook is added — the video opens straight on the character saying your first sentence, so lead with your strongest line.
en.arc: Follows your script sentence by sentence in order; each clip carries straight on from the previous one without restaging.
en.narrator: Exactly one character reads every line aloud to camera. Your script is used word for word; your separate instruction only guides tone and emphasis and is never spoken.
en.visual: Look and palette come from the chosen visual style. One locked full-body shot with the character centered and facing the camera; the same background, lighting and camera angle throughout. While speaking: continuous lip-sync, a small nod, a slight eyebrow lift, and one waist-height open-palm gesture. Feet stay planted.
en.audio: No background music — just the character's voice, with a bottom subtitle that matches each clip's spoken line exactly.
en.rules: Needs a script, one character image and an aspect ratio. Words are never rewritten. Short lines are grouped and long lines are split so each clip has a similar length. A script over 240 seconds must be shortened.
